papers.title: Cryogenic hydrogen embrittlement of 316plus (EN 1.4420) stainless steel at 77 K and 20 K
papers.abstract: This paper presents the first experimental characterisation of combined hydrogen-temperature effects in 316plus (EN 1.4420), a new austenitic stainless steel for liquid hydrogen (LH2) storage. Uniaxial tensile tests were conducted at room temperature (RT), 77 K and 20 K on uncharged and hydrogen-precharged specimens, complemented by fractography and EBSD-based quantification of strain-induced martensite (SIM). 316plus exhibited cryogenic strengthening at 77 K and 20 K by enhanced SIM formation. Hydrogen did not influence strength at RT or 77 K and caused a modest decrease (~10%) at 20 K, keeping 316plus at the upper bound of cryogenic strength for 316L. The presence of hydrogen resulted in significant reductions in ductility at all temperatures, being most severe at 77 and 20K (~40-50%). Hydrogen suppressed SIM at 20 K, but SIM fraction did not correlate with ductility reduction. Despite the combined effect of temperature and hydrogen, 316plus retained notable ductility (reduction in area ~30%).

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了316plus不锈钢在低温下的氢脆力学性能，但与增材制造（AM）工艺无关，仅作为材料背景参考。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing (AM) processing or AM-specific mechanical properties; it focuses on conventional wrought material under cryogenic hydrogen conditions.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究新型316plus不锈钢在液氢温度下的氢脆行为。
summary_zh.method: 在室温、77K和20K下对充氢和未充氢试样进行拉伸测试。
summary_zh.result: 氢降低了延展性（低温下~40-50%），但对强度影响小，材料仍保持一定延性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸实验、断口分析和EBSD表征验证。

summary_en.motivation: To characterize the combined effects of hydrogen and cryogenic temperature on the mechanical behavior of 316plus stainless steel for liquid hydrogen storage.
summary_en.method: Uniaxial tensile tests were performed at room temperature, 77 K, and 20 K on both hydrogen-precharged and uncharged specimens, supplemented by fractography and EBSD analysis.
summary_en.result: Hydrogen caused significant ductility loss (40–50%) at 77 K and 20 K but only a minor reduction in strength (10% at 20 K), while 316plus retained a reduction in area of approximately 30%.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through mechanical testing, fracture surface analysis, and quantitative EBSD phase mapping.
